text:
Mike: FYI customer reports 401s and huge retry/billing burn after upgrading our TS SDK to 2.0.0 in a Next.js SSR build. They say bundle picks the ESM entry and runtime ends up throwing at import time, then the app retries the request -> lots of duplicate billing.

Alice: ugh. do we have repro steps? which bundler / node version?

Mike: Next 13.4, webpack 5 (default), node 18.16.0. Repro steps they gave:
```
# minimal repro
npx create-next-app@13 my-app
npm i @redwood-inference/sdk@2.0.0
# server side fetch using our SDK during getServerSideProps
# build and run
next build && next start
```
They say errors only show up in prod build, dev mode is fine.

Sara: can you paste the runtime error / log?

Mike: log snippet they pasted: 
```
Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM]: Must use import to load ES Module: /app/node_modules/@redwood-inference/sdk/dist/esm/index.js
require() of ES modules is not supported.
    at Object.require (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:...)

Request to POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate returned 401 {"message":"Unauthorized","code":"invalid_api_key"}
SDK retry attempt 1 -> 401
SDK retry attempt 2 -> 401
... -> billing spike
```

John: that looks like the bundler resolved the package to the "exports" conditional -> esm entry. Next SSR expects a CJS-compatible entry unless you configure it. Do we ship a CJS fallback?

Alice: 2.0.0 changed package.json: moved main -> "dist/esm/index.js" and added conditional exports without a cjs fallback for older bundlers. snippet from package.json they sent: 
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

Sara: aha. older webpack + ts-loader sometimes prefers import entry and fails at runtime in SSR. Workarounds: 1) pin to 1.x which still had cjs entry, 2) consumer sets next.config.js webpack rule to prefer cjs, or 3) we publish a cjs fallback entry under "require" in exports.

Mike: customer tried pinning to 1.9.3 and issue resolved. But they want a long-term fix and we're getting escalated.

John: for short term I'd recommend publishing a patch (2.0.1) that adds a require conditional: 
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
    "types": "./dist/esm/index.d.ts"
  }
}
```
That should make bundlers that use require path pick the CJS build. Also make sure we ship dist/cjs with compiled .js and corresponding .d.ts.

Alice: also note types — pointing types at esm may confuse TS editors for consumers using cjs. We should provide a unified types entry (./dist/types/index.d.ts) or point both to the same declarations.

dev-bot: Incident created: INC-2023-1748, assigned to eng-packaging.

Sara: one more gotcha: some bundlers (esbuild, webpack 5) do fullySpecified resolution and may still pick the esm entry. Add docs recommending consumers set experimental: { esmExternals: 'loose' } in next.config.js or set webpack fallback: { 'node:module': false } is not ideal.

Mike: customer also reported the SDK retry loop made the 401s worse because our client retried on 401 by default for idempotent token refresh attempts. We should change retry policy: do not retry on auth 401. File an API/SDK change.

John: agreed. I'll open two PRs: packaging patch to add require cjs export + SDK change to stop auto-retrying on 401s. Also add test that installs the package in a minimal Next SSR app and runs build.

Alice: followups for support: ask the customer to temporarily pin to 1.9.3 and confirm. Offer a credit for the billing spike while we patch. Collect package-lock and reproduction repo if possible.

Mike: sent to customer: pin to 1.9.3, setting: next.config.js { experimental: { esmExternals: 'loose' } } as alternative. Waiting on confirm.

Sara: scope: eng-packaging to publish 2.0.1 with require export and dist/cjs ship. eng-runtime to change retry policy for 401. I'll track in INC-2023-1748 and notify support. :thumbsup:

John: PRs opened: #462-packaging-fix, #463-no-retry-on-401. Assign reviewers.

Mike: thanks team.
